fact: Le Quotidien reports the first phase of the national interoperability platform, UXP, was completed in 2025 in five ministries, with first applications deployed in 2024.
Le Quotidien reports a contract signed with Cybernetica for phase two, running to end-2027, to integrate the platform across all ministries.
Cybernetica states phase 1 introduced UXP to five key ministries and institutions.

Cybernetica states a phase 2 contract was signed with the Ministries of Communication Technologies and of Economy and Planification, extending the platform to RNE, TIA, APII, CEPEX, the Ministry of Finance and the Central Bank, scheduled to complete in 2027.
CNI's page describes a national X-Road interoperability platform with three pilot services (tax situation, death notification, payslip), without a date on the page; published date used.
Cybernetica states UXP was deployed as a proof of concept for five ministries, with the governing authority set up and five member organisations onboarded, in the go-live phase of Phase 1.

fact: The Ministry of Communication Technologies' workshop statement says the UXP national interconnection platform was presented and the project launched in a first phase with four ministries (Interior, Education, Transport, Social Affairs), to extend to the other ministries in a second phase; the page has no dateline, so the published year is used.

The Ministry of Communication Technologies presented the new national interoperability platform UXP at a workshop on 7 February 2024 and said the project was launched in a first phase with four ministries (Interior, Education, Transport, Social Affairs), to be extended to the other ministries in a second phase; the document does not say data is yet flowing.

The playbook names the Plateforme Nationale d'Interoperabilite, operated by the Centre National Informatique, carrying exchanges of citizen register data with state structures including civil status, schools, universities, vocational training and health, under decree-law 2020-31 and decree 2020-777.
A chart in the playbook shows exchanges of citizen register data with state structures rising from 476,052 to 900,125,547, the last of seven yearly values plotted for 2019-2025.

The deck lists setting up a national interoperability system on the Estonian X-Road model, and shows a National Interoperability Platform operated by the Centre National Informatique linking sector systems to the IUC.
